questions.q: What example did Hezekiah follow when he began to reign at the age of twenty-five?
questions.a: Hezekiah followed the example of his ancestor David and did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah tell the Levites to do after he had opened the doors of the house of Yahweh and had repaired them?
questions.a: Hezekiah told the Levites to consecrate themselves, consecrate the house of Yahweh, and carry away the filthiness from the holy place.

questions.q: What did their ancestors not do in the place where Yahweh lived?
questions.a: Their ancestors did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah say that their ancestors did in the sight of Yahweh?
questions.a: Hezekiah said that their ancestors trespassed and did what was evil in the sight of Yahweh their God.

questions.q: What was the result of Yahweh’s wrath falling on Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh made Judah and Jerusalem to be an object of terror, horror, and scorn.

questions.q: What happened to their fathers, sons, daughters, and wives because of the wrath of Yahweh?
questions.a: Their fathers fell by the sword and their sons, daughters, and wives were brought into captivity because of the wrath of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah propose to do so that Yahweh’s fierce anger might turn away from them?
questions.a: Hezekiah proposed that they make a covenant with Yahweh, the God of Israel.

questions.q: What did the Levites do after they gathered their brothers?
questions.a: The Levites and their brothers, dedicated themselves to Yahweh, and went in to cleanse the house of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did the priests do with all the filth that they found in the temple of Yahweh as they cleansed it?
questions.a: The priests took all the filth and carried it out to the brook Kidron.

questions.q: How long did it take the priests to sanctify the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: The priests began on the first day of the first month and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

questions.q: What did the priests tell Hezekiah they had prepared and sanctified in addition to cleansing all the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: In addition to cleansing all the house of Yahweh, the priests prepared and sanctified all the implements that King Ahaz threw away when he trespassed during his reign.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah command the priests to do with the animals they brought as a sin offering for Judah?
questions.a: Hezekiah told the priests to offer the animals on the altar of Yahweh.

questions.q: Why did the priests kill the animals and splash their blood on the altar?
questions.a: The priests killed the animals and splashed their blood on the altar to make atonement for all Israel. A burnt offering and a sin offering had to be made for all Israel.

questions.q: From whom did the command come for arranging the Levites and their instruments in the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: The command came from Yahweh by means of his prophets.

questions.q: How long did the singing and playing of music continue as all the assembly worshiped and the burnt offering began?
questions.a: The singing and music continued until the burnt offering was finished.

questions.q: What was the attitude of the Levites as they sang praises to Yahweh using the words of David and Asaph?
questions.a: The Levites sang praises with gladness and they bowed down and worshiped.

questions.q: What did the assembly bring into the house of Yahweh?
questions.a: The assembly brought in sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who had a willing heart brought burnt offerings.

questions.q: What kinds of animals did the assembly bring to be used as burnt offerings?
questions.a: The assembly brought bulls, rams, lambs, oxen, and sheep to be used as burnt offerings.

questions.q: Why did the priests have to ask the Levites to help skin the burnt offerings?
questions.a: The priests had to ask the Levites to help them skin the burnt offerings because the priests were too few to do the work themselves.

questions.q: What did Hezekiah and all the people do when the service of the house of Yahweh was set in order?
questions.a: Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced.

commentary.text: Verses 1–19 When Hezekiah came to the crown, he applied at once to work reform. Those who begin with God, begin at the right end of their work, and it will prosper accordingly. Those that turn their backs upon God's ordinances, may truly be said to forsake God himself. There are still such neglects, if the word be not duly read and opened, for that was signified by the lighting the lamps, and also if prayers and praise be not offered up, for that was signified by the burning incense. Neglect of God's worship was the cause of the calamities they had lain under. The Lord alone can prepare the heart of man for vital godliness: when much good is done in a little time, the glory must be ascribed to him; and all who love him or the souls of men, will rejoice therein. Let those that do good work, learn to do it well.

As soon as Hezekiah heard that the temple was ready, he lost no time. Atonement must be made for the sins of the last reign. It was not enough to lament and forsake those sins; they brought a sin-offering. Our repentance and reformation will not obtain pardon but in and through Christ, who was made sin, that is, a sin-offering for us. While the offerings were on the altar, the Levites sang. Sorrow for sin must not prevent us from praising God. The king and the congregation gave their consent to all that was done. It is not enough for us to be where God is worshipped, if we do not ourselves worship with the heart. And we should offer up our spiritual sacrifices of praise and thanksgiving, and devote ourselves and all we have, as sacrifices, acceptable to the Father only through the Redeemer.
